artifacts.notes: Establishes that ICEL is a mixed commission of eleven member conferences, that it is not itself a publisher, and that it provides content to the conferences, who authorise publishers. That is why a licence would have to be sought from ICEL and the position of a conference settled beside it.

passages.context: Read whole on 2026-08-01. Four things are established by the page's own words. (1) The acknowledgement ICEL requires for the Missal is 'The English translation of The Roman Missal (c) 2010, International Commission on English in the Liturgy Corporation. All rights reserved.', and for a partial use 'Excerpts from the English translation of The Roman Missal (c) 2010 ...'. (2) 'Liturgical texts are made available to publishers without distinction, on a non-exclusive basis. All requests for permission should be directed to the ICEL Secretariat' at a Washington address and at permission@eliturgy.org. (3) 'Any publication produced for sale which contains ICEL translations is subject to a royalty or flat fee', and the classes named include electronic media; publications not used during liturgical celebration -- textbooks, commentaries, religious education material, private prayerbooks, recordings -- 'may be assessed a royalty or flat fee'. (4) The one royalty-free class is narrow and does not reach a public corpus: reprinting 'in a publication for use at a specific Mass or celebration of an individual congregation or institution', on four conditions, that the publication is not produced by a publishing firm, is not sold, carries the copyright notice, and follows the official editions exactly.
passages.notes: A summary page. It links a fuller booklet of Publication Policies which this project has not retrieved, so nothing here is a complete statement of ICEL's terms; it is enough to establish that permission is required, that it is sought from the Secretariat, and that no existing exception covers a freely published web corpus of the orations.

work.description: The Commission's own public statement of who may reproduce its liturgical translations, on what terms, and with what acknowledgement. Registered because this repository's decision not to carry the approved English of the postconciliar Roman Missal rests on a rights position, and a rights position stated only in this project's prose is an assertion; stated against the rightsholder's own published terms it is evidence. ICEL is a mixed commission of eleven Catholic bishops' conferences, established at Rome in 1963 and erected as a mixed commission under Liturgiam authenticam on 15 September 2003; it is not a publisher and licenses its texts to publishers authorised by the conferences.
work.title: ICEL publication and copyright policies
